turnaround_reason: A former high-growth sleep-apnea implant darling fell from ~$147 to ~$61 on two fears: GLP-1s (Zepbound approved for OSA) cannibalizing candidates, and CMS/facility coding confusion around the new Inspire V. Thesis is that both are sentiment overhangs on a still-profitable, pristine-balance-sheet franchise.
bullish_points: Fortress balance sheet: cash $321M vs debt $29M, D/E 3.5, current ratio 8.5 — zero solvency risk, rare for a de-rated growth name
Actually profitable (profit margin ~15%) and beating: Q2 EPS 0.14 vs -0.25 est; prior two quarters also large beats
GLP-1 fear looks overblown: Inspire's own physician survey suggests GLP-1s expand OSA diagnosis funnel; many patients remain third-line implant candidates
Inspire V rollout + ambulatory surgery-center penetration are growth levers as CMS coding de-risks progressively through 2026
Sentiment washout: stock near 52w low ($61 vs low $39 / high $147), target mean $60.4 already reset low
bearish_points: Revenue is actually declining now (-7.6% TTM) — the growth story broke, this isn't just multiple compression
Still not cheap: fwd P/E ~39.5 embeds a re-acceleration that hasn't been proven
CMS/facility coding ambiguity for Inspire V is a real near-term revenue headwind; one analyst flags the overhang lasting into 2028
GLP-1 adoption trajectory is genuinely uncertain — if prescribers routinely try drugs first, the implant funnel slows for years
catalyst: Inspire V reimbursement/coding clarity plus a return to revenue growth confirming the GLP-1 fear was overdone
catalyst_timing: Q3 2026 earnings 2026-11-02; CMS coding updates through 2H 2026
suggested_trade: Small starter spot $58-61 with room to add on a coding-clarity catalyst or a growth-reacceleration print. Quality name at a washed-out sentiment level; size for the fact that revenue is still declining.
key_risk: GLP-1 substitution proves structural rather than complementary and Inspire V coding stays muddled, keeping revenue in decline and collapsing the growth multiple.
would_skip_if: Q3 revenue declines accelerate, or CMS coding resolution slips again with no reimbursement path in sight.
